commit_message:
[Torch] Convert torchao affine quantization to LinalgExt

Converts the typed torchao `quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine` ops
to `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine` during Torch
input conversion, reusing the PT2E conversion. Float zero points are
handled as for the PT2E ops. Also drops two includes from
`LinalgExtOps.cpp` that lost their users when `isKnownZero` moved to the
LinalgExt utils.

Depends on llvm/torch-mlir#4843 and a torch-mlir integrate.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: clang-tidy

"--define=iree_is_android=true" option in the bazel command line. This
change adds support for detecting Android also via setting a platform
with "@platforms//os:android".

commit_message:
[Torch] Drop all-zero float zero points of PT2E ops (#25112)

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports store those of symmetric
weights as float zeros. The conversion passed them to
`iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, which require
integer zero points, so the converted IR failed verification:

```
'iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine' op expected zero_point to have a signless integer element type, got 'f32'
```

- All-zero float zero points are now dropped like a `None` zero point.
- The check reuses `isKnownZero` from #24905, moved from
`LinalgExtOps.cpp` to the LinalgExt utils and extended to float splats.
- The per-channel, per-channel-group and per-token readers now read
their zero points through one helper.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: Analyze (actions)

[Torch] Drop all-zero float zero points of PT2E ops (#25112)

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports store those of symmetric
weights as float zeros. The conversion passed them to
`iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, which require
integer zero points, so the converted IR failed verification:

```
'iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine' op expected zero_point to have a signless integer element type, got 'f32'
```

- All-zero float zero points are now dropped like a `None` zero point.
- The check reuses `isKnownZero` from #24905, moved from
`LinalgExtOps.cpp` to the LinalgExt utils and extended to float splats.
- The per-channel, per-channel-group and per-token readers now read
their zero points through one helper.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Runtime][VM] connect ISA decoder validation macros and tighten register verification (#25088)

Tightens bytecode verification in
`runtime/src/iree/vm/bytecode/verifier.c` and `dispatch_util.h`:

- Route `IREE_VM_ISA_VALIDATE_REG_I32` in `dispatch_util.h` through
`IREE_VM_ISA_VERIFY_REG_I32(ordinal)` and check `ordinal <
verify_state->i32_register_count` instead of compiling to `((void)0)`,
and clamp `type_id` in `iree_vm_map_type` when `module->type_count ==
0`.
- Check register ordinals against the declared
`function_descriptor->i32_register_count` and `ref_register_count`
(matching the frame size allocated in `dispatch.c`) rather than rounding
counts up to a power of two during verification, and reject
`ref_register_count > IREE_VM_ISA_REF_REGISTER_MASK`.
- Reject cross-bank (`i32` vs `ref`) register pairs in
`iree_vm_bytecode_function_verify_remap_branch_operands`, decode
`DiscardRefs` with `VARIADIC_OPERANDS_REF`, and reject trailing `cconv`
signature characters past `reg_list->size` in
`iree_vm_bytecode_function_verify_cconv_registers`.
- Initialize function state in `assembler/parser.c` before parsing
function argument and result register lists so `ireec` counts unused
argument registers in function descriptors.
- Add unit tests in `runtime/src/iree/vm/bytecode/module_test.cc`
covering each verifier check.

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Separate ins and outs of Sort op

Currently, the Sort op is defined to take no ins() operands, and instead
takes the input tensors as outs(). After bufferization, it modifies
those outs() in-place. Not only is this inconsistent with other
LinalgExt ops, it also breaks some compiler invariants leading to bugs.

For that reason, we re-define the Sort op to take input tensors as ins()
and inits as outs(). Lit and E2E tests had to be converted to the new
syntax.

Assisted-by: Codex <noreply@openai.com>
Signed-off-by: Maksymilian B. Knust <knust@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Separate ins and outs of Sort op

Currently, the Sort op is defined to take no ins() operands, and instead
takes the input tensors as outs(). After bufferization, it modifies
those outs() in-place. Not only is this inconsistent with other
LinalgExt ops, it also breaks some compiler invariants leading to bugs.

For that reason, we re-define the Sort op to take input tensors as ins()
and inits as outs(). Lit and E2E tests had to be converted to the new
syntax.

commit_message:
[Torch] Drop all-zero float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports store the zero points of
symmetric weights as float zeros. The conversion passed them to
`iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, which require
integer zero points, so the converted IR failed verification. All-zero
float zero points are now dropped like a None zero point, and other
float zero points are left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering. The check
reuses `isKnownZero` from the zero-point canonicalization, moved to the
LinalgExt utils and extended to float splats. The per-channel,
per-channel-group and per-token readers now read their zero points
through one helper.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Torch] Drop all-zero float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports store the zero points of
symmetric weights as float zeros. The conversion passed them to
`iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, which require
integer zero points, so the converted IR failed verification. All-zero
float zero points are now dropped like a None zero point, and other
float zero points are left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering. The check
reuses `isKnownZero` from the zero-point canonicalization, moved to the
LinalgExt utils and extended to float splats. The per-channel,
per-channel-group and per-token readers now read their zero points
through one helper.

Part of #24862.

commit_message:
[Torch] Drop all-zero float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports store the zero points of
symmetric weights as float zeros. The conversion passed them to
`iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, which require
integer zero points, so the converted IR failed verification. All-zero
float zero points are now dropped like a None zero point, and other
float zero points are left for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering. The check
reuses `isKnownZero` from the zero-point canonicalization, moved to the
LinalgExt utils and extended to float splats. The per-channel,
per-channel-group and per-token readers now read their zero points
through one helper.

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Fold broadcasts into batch_matmul indexing maps

Replace ConvertBatchMatmulToMatmul, which rewrote
`batch_matmul(A, broadcast(B))` into collapse_shape + matmul +
expand_shape, with a pass that folds the broadcast into the batch_matmul's
indexing maps: the RHS map simply drops the batch dim. The collapse_shape
sat between a dequantize and its contraction and kept
ConvertQDQToIntegerMath from matching; now the contraction reads its
producers directly. CollapseDimensions turns the two-M-dim batch_matmul
into a plain matmul during dispatch creation, so codegen and data tiling
see the same op as before. The global optimization data tiling path sets
encodings before dispatch creation, so it now runs the standalone
contraction collapse first.

Broadcasts on either input fold, as linalg.broadcast or as a broadcasting
(and possibly transposing) generic, by composing maps, which also covers a
transposed LHS. Where the named op cannot express the folded map, as for a
batch-broadcast [N, K] weight that upstream's verifier rejects, the
contraction is carried by a linalg.generic with the same body instead of
moving data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Fold broadcasts into batch_matmul indexing maps

Replace ConvertBatchMatmulToMatmul, which rewrote
`batch_matmul(A, broadcast(B))` into collapse_shape + matmul +
expand_shape, with a pass that folds the broadcast into the batch_matmul's
indexing maps: the RHS map simply drops the batch dim. The collapse_shape
sat between a dequantize and its contraction and kept
ConvertQDQToIntegerMath from matching; now the contraction reads its
producers directly. CollapseDimensions turns the two-M-dim batch_matmul
into a plain matmul during dispatch creation, so codegen and data tiling
see the same op as before. The global optimization data tiling path sets
encodings before dispatch creation, so it now runs the standalone
contraction collapse first.

Broadcasts on either input fold, as linalg.broadcast or as a broadcasting
(and possibly transposing) generic, by composing maps, which also covers a
transposed LHS. Where the named op cannot express the folded map, as for a
batch-broadcast [N, K] weight that upstream's verifier rejects, the
contraction is carried by a linalg.generic with the same body instead of
moving data.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Collapse named contractions with user indexing maps

A linalg.batch_matmul whose RHS indexing map drops the batch dim (the
usual `x @ W` with a leading batch) was never collapsed: CollapseDimensions
only considered linalg.generic, and AnnotateDataTilingHints rejects the
resulting two-M-dim contraction. The same op written as a generic collapsed
to a 2-D matmul and was data-tiled, so data tiling depended on the named
vs. generic form, and on O2, where generalize-matmul hides the difference.

Make named contractions with projected-permutation maps eligible for
collapsing, in dispatch regions and in the standalone contraction collapse
pass, and generalize them before collapsing: upstream's named-op collapse
path clones the op with collapsed operands, which is only valid when the
collapse keeps the op's structure (e.g. linalg.fill). Named contractions
with their default maps have no collapsible loops and are unaffected, and
ones carrying a compilation_info or lowering_config keep their loop space,
as that configuration refers to the original loops.

Fixes #25110.

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert integral float zero points of PT2E ops

PT2E accepts float zero points, and exports store the zero points of
symmetric weights as float zeros. The conversion passed them to
`iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine`, which require
integer zero points, so the converted IR failed verification. Constant
float zero points with integer values within the bounds now convert
exactly: all-zero ones are dropped and others become i32 constants.
Fractional and non-constant float zero points are left for the
Torch-to-Linalg lowering.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Runtime][VM] connect ISA decoder validation macros and tighten register verification (#25088)

Tightens bytecode verification in
`runtime/src/iree/vm/bytecode/verifier.c` and `dispatch_util.h`:

- Route `IREE_VM_ISA_VALIDATE_REG_I32` in `dispatch_util.h` through
`IREE_VM_ISA_VERIFY_REG_I32(ordinal)` and check `ordinal <
verify_state->i32_register_count` instead of compiling to `((void)0)`,
and clamp `type_id` in `iree_vm_map_type` when `module->type_count ==
0`.
- Check register ordinals against the declared
`function_descriptor->i32_register_count` and `ref_register_count`
(matching the frame size allocated in `dispatch.c`) rather than rounding
counts up to a power of two during verification, and reject
`ref_register_count > IREE_VM_ISA_REF_REGISTER_MASK`.
- Reject cross-bank (`i32` vs `ref`) register pairs in
`iree_vm_bytecode_function_verify_remap_branch_operands`, decode
`DiscardRefs` with `VARIADIC_OPERANDS_REF`, and reject trailing `cconv`
signature characters past `reg_list->size` in
`iree_vm_bytecode_function_verify_cconv_registers`.
- Initialize function state in `assembler/parser.c` before parsing
function argument and result register lists so `ireec` counts unused
argument registers in function descriptors.
- Add unit tests in `runtime/src/iree/vm/bytecode/module_test.cc`
covering each verifier check.

This LLVM integration goes to just before "910cdcd09377 PassBuilder: Take LLVMContext for LibraryOptionsContext (#233150)", because this commit requires bigger work in IREE to reorganize the handling of global pass options on the command line.

Due to "45b9b97b83db [mlir][tosa][NFC] Speed up compilation of TosaProfileCompliance (#233949)" addressing the stacke usage, the increase of the MSVC stack limit for compiler tools in "58c31ac5c8 Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@6be022066fd2 (#25045)" can be taken out again here.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expand QDQ contractions over collapsed operands (#25086)

Fixes #25085

The frontend dequantizes both operands per block as `[M, G, L]` and `[N,
G, L]` and collapses them back to `[*, K]` before the matmul. The weight
is also transposed:

```mlir
%a  = iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine ... -> tensor<?x2x32xf32>
%ac = tensor.collapse_shape %a [[0], [1, 2]] : tensor<?x2x32xf32> into tensor<?x64xf32>
%b  = iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine ... -> tensor<8x2x32xf32>
%bc = tensor.collapse_shape %b [[0], [1, 2]] : tensor<8x2x32xf32> into tensor<8x64xf32>
%bt = linalg.transpose ins(%bc : tensor<8x64xf32>) ... permutation = [1, 0]
%c  = linalg.matmul ins(%ac, %bt : tensor<?x64xf32>, tensor<64x8xf32>) ...
```

The `collapse_shape` hid the dequantize from the integer rewrite.
`PropagateAffineQuantization` now adds the upstream
`linalg::populateFoldReshapeOpsByExpansionPatterns`, with a control
function that accepts only a `collapse_shape` of a dequantize consumed
by:

- a `linalg.transpose`. The collapse moves after the transpose, and the
existing transpose fusion folds the transpose into the dequantize's
output map.
- a contraction whose inputs are all dequantized, directly or through a
`collapse_shape`. The contraction expands to iterate over `(m, n, g,
l)`. The `expand_shape`s inserted on its other inputs cancel their
`collapse_shape`s, so the contraction reads both dequantizes directly.
The integer rewrite then reduces each block in i32 and sums the blocks
in floating point.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expand QDQ contractions over collapsed operands (#25086)

Fixes #25085

The frontend dequantizes both operands per block as `[M, G, L]` and `[N,
G, L]` and collapses them back to `[*, K]` before the matmul. The weight
is also transposed:

```mlir
%a  = iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine ... -> tensor<?x2x32xf32>
%ac = tensor.collapse_shape %a [[0], [1, 2]] : tensor<?x2x32xf32> into tensor<?x64xf32>
%b  = iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine ... -> tensor<8x2x32xf32>
%bc = tensor.collapse_shape %b [[0], [1, 2]] : tensor<8x2x32xf32> into tensor<8x64xf32>
%bt = linalg.transpose ins(%bc : tensor<8x64xf32>) ... permutation = [1, 0]
%c  = linalg.matmul ins(%ac, %bt : tensor<?x64xf32>, tensor<64x8xf32>) ...
```

The `collapse_shape` hid the dequantize from the integer rewrite.
`PropagateAffineQuantization` now adds the upstream
`linalg::populateFoldReshapeOpsByExpansionPatterns`, with a control
function that accepts only a `collapse_shape` of a dequantize consumed
by:

- a `linalg.transpose`. The collapse moves after the transpose, and the
existing transpose fusion folds the transpose into the dequantize's
output map.
- a contraction whose inputs are all dequantized, directly or through a
`collapse_shape`. The contraction expands to iterate over `(m, n, g,
l)`. The `expand_shape`s inserted on its other inputs cancel their
`collapse_shape`s, so the contraction reads both dequantizes directly.
The integer rewrite then reduces each block in i32 and sums the blocks
in floating point.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking

Executable objects that carry inline data got a temporary file path,
but the data was never written to it.

The linker then received an empty object file.

Serialize the object data into the temporary file and report an error
if that fails.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@github.com>

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert torchao affine quantization to LinalgExt

Converts the typed torchao `quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine` ops
to `iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine` / `dequantize_affine` during Torch
input conversion, reusing the PT2E conversion. Float zero points are
handled as for the PT2E ops. Also drops two includes from
`LinalgExtOps.cpp` that lost their users when `isKnownZero` moved to the
LinalgExt utils.

Depends on llvm/torch-mlir#4843 and a torch-mlir integrate.

Part of #24862.

Signed-off-by: Roberto Laudani <laudani@roofline.ai>
name: linux_x64_bazel / linux_x64_bazel

commit_message:
[bazel] detect Android also via the selected build platform (#25107)

The bazel build used to support android only via a dedicated
"--define=iree_is_android=true" option in the bazel command line. This
change adds support for detecting Android also via setting a platform
with "@platforms//os:android".
